subject: learned response with behaviour learned from another project

messages.author: 91bd4367f6044e8d
messages.subject: learned response with behaviour learned from another project
parts:
Hi,

I'm working with animals that have been subjected to cage-trapping at either other sites or by other projects. Is there a way to include being a 'recaptured' animal from occasion one?

Thanks,

Rebecca

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: learned response with behaviour learned from another project
parts:
If the carried over effect is permanent throughout your present study I suppose you could just use a 2-level individual covariate (and conditional likelihood). Are you are wanting to combine prior experience and transitions from naive to experienced in the current study?
Murray

parts: A persistent effect, so if we imagine it as a covariate some animals that have been caught at least once in their life would have a '1' for recap on occasion 1, whilst animals which had never been caught in their life would be '0' on first capture. messages.subject: Re: learned response with behaviour learned from another project
parts:
I replied a couple of hours ago but I can't see my post - it seems to have been lost - so here is most of it again. See words and code in attached pdf. Code to hack the design data frame looks like this:

makedf.b2 <- function (ch, nmix = 1) {
    recap <- covariates(ch)$recap
    if (is.null(recap)) stop ("expecting binary individual covariate 'recap'")
    # Construct matrix of logical values for a standard learned response 'b'
    # TRUE iff caught before
    detected <- apply(abs(ch),1:2,sum)>0
    detected <- t(apply(detected, 1, cumsum)>0)
    # Force codes for experienced animals to TRUE across all occasions
    detected[recap>0,] <- TRUE  
    b <- t(apply(detected, 1, function(x) {x[which.max(x)] <- FALSE; x}))
    n <- nrow(ch)
    S <- ncol(ch)
    K <- dim(ch)[3]
    data.frame(customb = insertdim(b, 1:2, c(n,S,K,nmix)))  
}

# test on phony data (40% experienced animals)
testCH <- captdata
detector(traps(testCH)) <- 'multi'
# randomly assign code for previous experience
covariates(testCH) <- data.frame(recap = sample(0:1, nrow(testCH), replace = TRUE,
                                                prob = c(0.6,0.4)))
fitb <- secr.fit(testCH, model = g0 ~ b, CL = TRUE, trace = FALSE)
# note use of column name 'customb' and dframe specification
fitb2 <- secr.fit(testCH, model = g0 ~ customb, dframe = makedf.b2(testCH), CL = TRUE,
                  trace = FALSE)
AIC(fitb, fitb2)

On Monday, 28 May 2018 21:13:48 UTC+10, Murray Efford wrote:
I replied a couple of hours ago but I can't see my post - it seems to have been lost - so here is most of it again. See words and code in attached pdf. Code to hack the design data frame looks like this:

makedf.b2 <- function (ch, nmix = 1) {
    recap <- covariates(ch)$recap
    if (is.null(recap)) stop ("expecting binary individual covariate 'recap'")
    # Construct matrix of logical values for a standard learned response 'b'
    # TRUE iff caught before
    detected <- apply(abs(ch),1:2,sum)>0
    detected <- t(apply(detected, 1, cumsum)>0)
    # Force codes for experienced animals to TRUE across all occasions
    detected[recap>0,] <- TRUE  
    b <- t(apply(detected, 1, function(x) {x[which.max(x)] <- FALSE; x}))
    n <- nrow(ch)
    S <- ncol(ch)
    K <- dim(ch)[3]
    data.frame(customb = insertdim(b, 1:2, c(n,S,K,nmix)))  
}

# test on phony data (40% experienced animals)
testCH <- captdata
detector(traps(testCH)) <- 'multi'
# randomly assign code for previous experience
covariates(testCH) <- data.frame(recap = sample(0:1, nrow(testCH), replace = TRUE,
                                                prob = c(0.6,0.4)))
fitb <- secr.fit(testCH, model = g0 ~ b, CL = TRUE, trace = FALSE)
# note use of column name 'customb' and dframe specification
fitb2 <- secr.fit(testCH, model = g0 ~ customb, dframe = makedf.b2(testCH), CL = TRUE,
                  trace = FALSE)
AIC(fitb, fitb2)
